record.summary: Spice Route Cafés entered a nine‑year lease with Meridian Estates in 2019 for a ground‑floor unit. The lease was amended three times: to extend the fit‑out period, to reduce rent for six months (Amendment 2, Oct 2021), and to add a storage room (Amendment 3). Meridian now claims Spice Route has underpaid rent by ₹7,20,000 for the past two years and threatens termination. Spice Route argues the rent reduction was to be followed by the original rent schedule without back‑charging and that Meridian’s calculation double‑counts the 5% escalation. Meridian says the reduction was a one‑time concession and that escalation compounds from the original rent. The breach notice was sent by email only, although the lease requires registered post, and the 30‑day cure period has not yet elapsed.
record.goal: Determine whether Meridian’s termination notice is legally valid and who is correct on the rent‑escalation calculation.
questions: What are the exact dates (or at least month and year) of Amendment 1 (fit‑out extension) and Amendment 3 (storage room addition)?
On what date was the later email from Meridian’s property manager (the waiver) sent?
When exactly was the breach notice emailed, and was any registered‑post notice also sent?
Did Spice Route raise any objection in writing to the April 2022 email about the escalated rent?
Has Meridian formally invoked the 30‑day cure period under clause 18 after sending the breach notice?
contradictions: Clause 25 requires breach notice by registered post, but Meridian sent only an email.
Amendment 2 does not specify whether the 5% escalation applies during the six‑month reduced rent period, leading to differing interpretations.
The waiver email was not signed; clause 22 says amendments (including waivers) need signatures from both parties.
evidence: Lease clause 4.2 – annual escalation of 5% "on the rent then payable".
Lease clause 18 – default and 30‑day cure period.
Lease clause 22 – amendments effective only if signed by both parties.
Lease clause 25 – notice of breach must be sent by registered post.
Email (April 2022) – rent from May at escalated rate.
Email (later) – waiver of chase for reduced‑period difference.

events.description: Spice Route Cafés signed a nine‑year lease for a 2,400 sq ft ground‑floor unit with Meridian Estates, with a base rent and a 5% annual escalation.
Amendment 1 executed to extend the fit‑out period.
events.day: Date of first amendment not specified

events.description: Amendment 2 signed, reducing rent by 30% for six months and stating that rent shall revert to the amount payable under the lease thereafter. No explicit wording on whether the 5% escalation continues during the reduced period.
Amendment 3 added a second storage room with a fixed monthly sum; all other terms unchanged.
events.day: Date of third amendment not specified

events.description: Meridian’s accountant emailed that rent from May will be at the escalated rate as per schedule.
Spice Route paid the escalated rent amount for 14 consecutive months without objection.
Meridian’s property manager emailed that they would not chase the difference from the reduced period.
Meridian sent a breach notice by email, claiming underpayment of ₹7,20,000 over two years and threatening termination and forfeiture of the security deposit.
